statement: Let ones(x) be the number of 1 digits in the standard binary representation of the nonnegative integer x (so ones(0) = 0). The function returns a result r such that: (1) len(r) = len(arr); (2) r is a permutation of arr, meaning that for every integer v, the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(r) and r[i] = v equals the number of indices j with 0 <= j < len(arr) and arr[j] = v; and (3) for all i and j with 0 <= i < j < len(r), either ones(r[i]) < ones(r[j]), or ones(r[i]) = ones(r[j]) and r[i] <= r[j]. Thus r is exactly the sequence obtained by sorting arr in nondecreasing order of the pair (ones(x), x).
preconditions: len(arr) >= 1 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), arr[i] >= 0.

statement: The function returns a result r for every arr satisfying the preconditions; in particular it does not fail, panic, overflow, or perform an out-of-bounds access.
preconditions: len(arr) >= 1 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), arr[i] >= 0.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, len(r) = len(arr).
preconditions: len(arr) >= 1 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), arr[i] >= 0.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every integer v, the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(r) and r[i] = v equals the number of indices j with 0 <= j < len(arr) and arr[j] = v.
preconditions: len(arr) >= 1 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), arr[i] >= 0.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every integer b >= 0, the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(r) and ones(r[i]) = b equals the number of indices j with 0 <= j < len(arr) and ones(arr[j]) = b, where ones(x) is the number of 1 digits in the binary representation of the nonnegative integer x.
preconditions: len(arr) >= 1 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), arr[i] >= 0.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every k with 0 <= k and k+1 < len(r), ones(r[k]) <= ones(r[k+1]), where ones(x) is the number of 1 digits in the binary representation of the nonnegative integer x.
preconditions: len(arr) >= 1 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), arr[i] >= 0.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for all i and j with 0 <= i < j < len(r), if ones(r[i]) = ones(r[j]) then r[i] <= r[j], where ones(x) is the number of 1 digits in the binary representation of the nonnegative integer x.
preconditions: len(arr) >= 1 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), arr[i] >= 0.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for all i and j with 0 <= i < j < len(r), either ones(r[i]) < ones(r[j]), or ones(r[i]) = ones(r[j]) and r[i] <= r[j], where ones(x) is the number of 1 digits in the binary representation of the nonnegative integer x.
preconditions: len(arr) >= 1 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), arr[i] >= 0.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every k with 0 <= k < len(r), min(arr) <= r[k] <= max(arr), where min(arr) is the least entry of the nonempty array arr and max(arr) is the greatest entry of arr.
preconditions: len(arr) >= 1 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), arr[i] >= 0.

statement: Whenever the function returns result r1 for arr1 and result r2 for arr2, r1 = r2.
preconditions: len(arr1) >= 1, len(arr2) >= 1, every entry of arr1 and arr2 is nonnegative, and for every integer v the number of occurrences of v in arr1 equals the number of occurrences of v in arr2.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every integer v, v occurs in r if and only if v occurs in arr, where v occurs in a sequence s if there exists an index k with 0 <= k < len(s) and s[k] = v.
preconditions: len(arr) >= 1 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), arr[i] >= 0.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every integer v, the set of indices k with 0 <= k < len(r) and r[k] = v is a contiguous interval of indices: if 0 <= i < j < k < len(r), r[i] = v, and r[k] = v, then r[j] = v.
preconditions: len(arr) >= 1 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), arr[i] >= 0.
